Venezuela Appoints New Executive Vice President at Petroleos de Venezuela SA

CARACAS, June 19 — Venezuela’s government has appointed María Fernanda Ríos as executive vice president of state-run oil company Petroleos de Venezuela SA, according to an official statement released Wednesday, marking the latest leadership change at the heart of the country’s vital energy sector.

Ríos, a petroleum engineer with over two decades of experience in Venezuela’s oil industry, previously held senior roles at several regional production units and served as a technical adviser to the Ministry of Petroleum. She takes over the executive vice presidency amid efforts by the government to bolster operational efficiency and reinforce internal management practices at the company.

“María Fernanda Ríos brings a blend of technical expertise and operational leadership that will be essential in advancing our strategic priorities,” Oil Minister Rafael Tellez said in the statement. “We are confident that her appointment will strengthen our ongoing modernization initiatives at Petroleos de Venezuela SA.”

The appointment, effective immediately, was approved by the company’s board of directors following consultations with senior government officials. Ríos replaces Luis Manuel Ortega, who has retired after five years in the post.

Industry analysts say the move reflects a broader strategy to rejuvenate the upper management ranks at Venezuela’s state energy firms. “PDVSA’s leadership transitions typically signal a focus on continuity and the need to address operational challenges,” said Carlos Pérez, an energy analyst at Caracas-based consultancy Grupo Energiar. “Ríos is well regarded for her experience in upstream operations and her track record of improving project delivery timelines.”

Petroleos de Venezuela SA, known as PDVSA, remains the country’s primary source of export revenue and a cornerstone of the Venezuelan economy. According to government data, the company produced an average of 835,000 barrels per day in May, with most output destined for Asian and Caribbean markets.

A spokesperson for the PDVSA Workers’ Federation welcomed the announcement and called for continued dialogue between management and employees. “We look forward to working with the new executive vice president to further strengthen our workplace and maintain steady operations,” said union representative Alfredo Domínguez.

Ríos is expected to meet with senior staff and union leaders at PDVSA headquarters in Caracas later this week.
